strategy.title: No plan for $500,000: the registry holds too few buyers at the evidenced $300 price

reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE is justified. Every chain link rests on this offer's own evidence: price $300 is what 43 distinct centre directors actually paid through the checkout (payment processor records, 2026-11) - a real purchase price by this buyer population, so the disagreement with Brain's 'no single price' basis is correct (the card holds priceCents 30000 and an EVIDENCE price fact); conversion 43/300 = 14.3% measured on this offer; 1,100 uncontacted registry directors (1,400 listed, 300 contacted, one purchase a year each) is a counted population; Brain produces the spreadsheet at $5; cash usable 3 days after payment; $0 capital tied up. Recomputed: 150 x 0.1433 = 21.5 expected sales; 21 x $300 = $6,300 >= $6,000; direct cost 21 x $5 = $105 paid from settled receipts on day 8, so no up-front capital; proof day 8 of 30.
findings: Price is a purchase price paid by 43 buyers of exactly this kind, not a benchmark or a single organisation; OFFER_AND_PRICE disagreement is well founded.

Margin is thin at 150 contacts: the target needs 20 sales; with n=150, p=0.143 (mean 21.5, sd ~4.3) the chance of >=20 is only about 2 in 3. Outreach costs $0 and 1,100 contacts are available, so the REACH step should continue (e.g. 200-250 contacts, or until 20 paid) rather than stop at 150 - an execution note, not a chain gap.
The 300 already contacted may have been the most responsive; conversion on the remaining registry could be lower - another reason to size outreach with headroom.
Executor capabilities SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE show NOT_CONNECTED; payment uses the existing checkout link, but sending the outreach needs the send capability connected before day 1.
Ledger matches the steps: one receipt of $6,300 settling day 8, one $105 spend after settlement; net $6,195; nothing unknown treated as known.

reviews.reasons: The contract changed to $500,000 in 30 days (version 2) and the revision correctly moves to NO_PLAN. At the evidenced $300 purchase price (43 paid checkouts), $500,000 needs ceil(500000/300) = 1,667 sales, while the counted population is 1,400 registry centres buying once a year, 300 already contacted. Even 100% of the 1,100 uncontacted gives $330,000 (all 1,400: $420,000); at the measured 43/300 = 14.33% conversion, 1,100 x 0.1433 = ~158 sales = ~$47,300. That is a real constraint - all the evidence together cannot fit the target - stated as TARGET with basis buyerVolume and price, and the decisive link is MARKET_VOLUME. The resolution (lower the target to ~$47k, or discover further populations / higher-priced offers) is right, and prior review findings are answered.
findings: Recomputed: 1,667 sales needed vs 1,100 uncontacted (1,400 total) buyers at one purchase a year; ceiling $330,000 (uncontacted) / $420,000 (all), measured-conversion yield ~$47,300.
Price remains a real purchase price paid by 43 buyers of this kind; the OFFER_AND_PRICE disagreement with Brain's 'no single price' basis is still well founded.
No spend and no outreach steps, consistent with $0 exposure.
